output.evidence: Version 1 (image 5) delivers the declared slate concept most faithfully: the cleft slate wall shows genuine natural cleavage grain and fracture planes, with a soft diagonal sweep reading from the upper left across the stone. The left text block (sans hierarchy TOM FORD / TOBACCO VANILLE / EAU DE PARFUM) sits in the upper-left half, its thin white rule landing exactly at the bottle's shoulder line as a chiseled baseline, preserving the beside layout and asymmetric stone-carved grid. The bottle is a recognizable, cleanly lit hero with legible gold label, matte stone versus glossy glass tactile contrast, and no studio gear. Version 2 (image 6) instead introduces a raised slate ledge behind the bottle while the packshot floats in front of it with its base hanging below the shelf edge and no contact shadow, the named defect; its stone also reads flatter and more uniform, weakening the cleft-cleavage character.
remaining_problems: Version 1's bottle still reads as a wall-mounted cutout: no contact shadow or grounding plane ties it physically to the slate, so contact conviction is implied rather than proven
The diagonal light sweep is subtle and slightly competes with the natural cleavage diagonals, making the sweep direction less legible than intended
Text block vertical overlap with the shoulder line is achieved only via the baseline rule; the type group itself stops above the shoulder, leaving the left column slightly top-weighted
